title: Aunt Lou Has A Key To YOURS 🔑
premise: My aunt Lou, the locksmith of our court of twelve houses, has a key to every one of them. For a month every door has clicked at midnight and again before sunrise, and the neighbors think she lets herself in. I moved into number seven last month and never gave her a key. She has one anyway, and my sneakers are wet every morning, so I put a camera on my porch.
twist: The thing that walks the court at midnight trying every handle is me, asleep, sleepwalking back to my old room at Aunt Lou's. She locks ten doors every night so the only handle I can open is hers, then walks me home and locks my door behind me. We carry my old bed and lamp across the court, and I stop walking.
world: a closed court of twelve narrow red-brick houses in a horseshoe round a teal-lit stone fountain, ivy, iron lamps, brass handles and numeral plates, a locksmith's key shop window, and a porch camera's night footage
